responsibility: Implements rustc’s built-in macro and compiler-injected attribute expansion layer: the crate root (`lib.rs`) declares the implementation modules, loads diagnostics, and registers all built-in bang macros, attributes, derives, and the proc-macro-backed `quote!` entry point with the resolver. It provides front ends and expanders for assertion and panic-related syntax through `assert.rs` plus the richer generic assertion machinery in the `assert` module, and edition-aware panic forwarding in `edition_panic.rs`; for configuration-driven syntax through `cfg.rs`, `cfg_accessible.rs`, `cfg_eval.rs`, and command-line crate attribute injection in `cmdline_attrs.rs`; for immediate compile-time feedback through `compile_error.rs`, debugging aids in `log_syntax.rs` and `trace_macros.rs`, and common helper routines in `util.rs`. The crate handles compile-time literal and identifier construction macros via `concat.rs`, `concat_bytes.rs`, and `concat_idents.rs`; environment and source introspection/inclusion macros via `env.rs` and `source_util.rs`; formatting support via `format.rs`, which parses and validates `format_args!`-family invocations into `FormatArgs` AST, the `format` module, which lowers the parsed model into `core::fmt::Arguments` construction, and `format_foreign.rs` plus the `format_foreign` module, which parse, translate, and test printf- and shell-style foreign format syntaxes used in diagnostics. It supplies built-in derive handling through `derive.rs`, which validates and schedules derive expansion, and the `deriving` module, which contains the shared derive synthesis framework and trait-specific generators for standard, marker, and legacy serialization derives. It also implements compiler-recognized attributes that synthesize runtime integration shims, including `alloc_error_handler.rs` for allocation-failure handling, `global_allocator.rs` for allocator entry points, and `standard_library_imports.rs` for implicit `std`/`core`/prelude imports. Finally, it supports test and proc-macro crate construction through `test.rs` and `test_harness.rs` for collecting tests and generating the test runner, and `proc_macro_harness.rs` for discovering proc-macro entry points and synthesizing the exported harness. Overall, this crate is the compiler component that expands Rust’s built-in macros and attributes, injects required compiler-generated items, and bridges parsed macro syntax into the AST forms and runtime hooks the rest of rustc relies on.
